_about: Plain-English summaries for the README catalog, read by scripts/gen-readme.py. The `description:` in each command/skill is written for Claude (it decides when the skill fires) and comes from ~/.claude via /sync-claude-slash; these summaries are written for people and live only here. One sentence, about 150 characters at most, no trigger phrases or internal paths.

groups.title: Ship and save work
groups.blurb: Get work committed, merged and safely parked.

groups.title: Plan and pick work back up
groups.blurb: Know what's left, what's next, and what's waiting on you.

groups.title: Deploy hardening
groups.blurb: The `harden-*` series: checks to run before something goes live. `/harden-for-deploy` runs the eight numbered steps in order.

groups.title: Repo health and cleanup
groups.blurb: One-repo audits and fixes for cruft, risk and dead weight.

groups.title: Weekly sweeps across your repos
groups.blurb: Each sweep works through your most recently used repos one at a time, keeping a progress file so it can stop and resume. None of them commit or push.

groups.title: Pages and UI polish
groups.blurb: Build and improve web pages and app screens. The page builders keep a scorecard, and a new version only counts if it beats the best one so far.

groups.title: Build features and tests
groups.blurb: Plan and build new work, with tests.

groups.title: App building blocks
groups.blurb: The `apply-*` series adds a proven piece from my other apps to this one, adapted to its stack. Each one skips what's already there.

groups.title: Hand a repo to another team
groups.blurb: For a repo that's going into someone else's environment.

groups.title: Your Claude setup
groups.blurb: For the Claude Code setup itself and the Mac it runs on.

groups.title: MCP servers
groups.blurb: Small local servers that give Claude extra tools. Setup is in [mcp-servers/README.md](mcp-servers/README.md).

commands/shipit.summary: Commits your work, merges it into main and pushes, then deletes the branch. If anything looks off, it stops and tells you where things are.

commands/stash.summary: Moves a file Claude just made into a shared holding area so you can pull it into another repo. The holding area empties nightly.

commands/unstash.summary: Drops the most recently stashed file into the current repo.

commands/handoff-to-next.summary: Writes a dated note on what happened this session so the next session, or person, can pick up cold. Runs only when you ask.

commands/roadmap.summary: Makes one ROADMAP.md the only list of what's left, folds other plan docs into it, and adds a check that catches the roadmap falling behind.

commands/cleanup-roadmap.summary: For coming back to a project: commits leftover work if it builds, prunes finished and stale roadmap items, then ships.

commands/rediscover.summary: Looks over the repo and tells you the single best next thing to do. Changes nothing.

commands/ask-me.summary: Finds the few open decisions actually blocking work in this repo and asks you them with real options, then records your answers.

commands/pathfinder.summary: Suggests a ranked list of features worth adding, each backed by evidence from the code. Changes nothing.

skills/build-status.summary: A live page in your browser showing how a build is going: steps done and left, recent commits, test status, findings, and questions for you.

skills/lead-keeper.summary: One session that watches every build-status page on this Mac, passes your messages to each build and brings their replies back.

commands/harden-for-deploy.summary: Runs all eight harden steps in order and writes one report. Stops early on anything critical. Never deploys.

commands/harden-secrets.summary: Step 1: looks for leaked passwords and API keys in the code and its git history.

commands/harden-auth.summary: Step 2: reviews login, sessions and permissions for weak spots such as insecure cookies or unprotected routes.

commands/harden-deps.summary: Step 3: checks dependencies for known vulnerabilities, separating what ships to production from dev-only tools.

commands/harden-licenses.summary: Step 4: lists every dependency's license and flags any that clash with yours, such as GPL code inside an MIT project.

commands/harden-config.summary: Step 5: checks deploy settings for the target (Railway, npm or public GitHub): health check, license, README, no internal hostnames.

commands/harden-lint.summary: Step 6: makes sure a linter and type checker are set up and passing, without silencing rules to get there.

commands/harden-tests.summary: Step 7: finds important code with no tests (login, payments, data writes) and writes tests for the biggest gaps.

commands/harden-observability.summary: Step 8: checks that errors get logged, nothing fails silently, and there's a health-check endpoint.

commands/front-door-security.summary: A quick security pass on what outsiders can reach: fixes what's safe to fix and flags leaked keys that need replacing.

commands/cleanup-repo.summary: Finds stale files, committed junk, leaked secrets and .gitignore gaps, and writes a cleanup plan. Deletes nothing.

commands/lowhangingfruit.summary: Finds easy cleanup wins, shows you the top three, and does the ones you approve.

commands/audit-burden.summary: Finds features that cost more than they're worth and traces each to the conversation that added it. Changes nothing.

commands/update-deps.summary: Updates Node dependencies safely: asks before big upgrades, runs your checks, and offers to roll back if anything breaks.

commands/port-collision-scan.summary: Finds local projects that try to use the same network port and writes a fix-up plan for each clash.

commands/generate-port-registry.summary: Gives every local project its own port, recorded in one file, and installs the port-registry server so new projects get one automatically.

commands/get-network-logs.summary: Pulls a deployed app's access logs and works out who's visiting (people, bots or scanners) and from where.

skills/autonomous-sweep-core.summary: The shared engine the other sweeps are built on. You rarely run it directly.

skills/autonomous-doc-refresh.summary: Fixes docs that no longer match the code, checking every claim against the source first.

skills/brand-scrub-sweep.summary: Finds real company names that slipped into docs where a codename belongs, and scrubs the accidental ones.

skills/changelog-refresh.summary: Writes a CHANGELOG.md where one is missing and adds entries for releases it hasn't covered yet.

skills/config-drift.summary: Finds settings that have drifted: env vars missing from .env.example, unpinned versions, lockfiles out of step.

skills/deadlink-check.summary: Finds broken links in docs, fixes the internal ones it can, and flags dead external ones.

skills/deploy-health.summary: Checks deployed services (mainly Railway) for failed deploys, errors, slowdowns, crash loops and stale code. Report only.

skills/license-compliance.summary: Checks each repo's license and flags dependencies whose licenses conflict with it.

skills/security-sweep.summary: Looks for leaked secrets and vulnerable dependencies and reports them. Never rewrites history or upgrades anything.

skills/test-backfill.summary: Writes tests for important untested code, using each repo's existing test setup.

skills/wip-reconciler.summary: Finds work at risk of being lost (uncommitted changes, stashes, unpushed branches) and gives you the commands to rescue it.

commands/gen-sys-doc.summary: Reads the whole repo and writes one system design document with diagrams, checking every diagram and link.

commands/gen-sdd-doc.summary: Writes a Solution Design Document for engineering leads and reviewers: architecture, decisions and risks, fact-checked.

commands/diagramsystemflow.summary: Traces how requests and jobs flow through the code and draws it, with every step pointing to a file and line.

commands/update-docs.summary: Checks the docs against the actual code and fixes what's out of date. Doesn't commit.

commands/generate-build-report.summary: Writes BUILD_REPORT.md: how this repo was built, from Claude session logs and git history, with an honest look back.

skills/enrich-document.summary: Adds a table of contents, cross-links, links to the tools it names, and copy-a-prompt buttons to a document.

skills/plain-walkthrough.summary: Explains a complicated system to non-engineers in one page: a real example walked step by step, plus a short glossary.

commands/generate-journey-page.summary: Builds a new one-page, scroll-driven explainer on a topic. Each new page has to beat the best one so far.

commands/level-up-page.summary: Makes a better version of an existing web page as a new file. Each version has to beat the last.

commands/plain-cut.summary: Makes a plain-language version of an overbuilt page: half the words, simpler figures. The original stays untouched.

commands/uxrefine.summary: Polishes an app's look and feel on a separate branch (layout, spacing, empty and error states, accessibility) without changing behavior.

commands/frontendtailwind.summary: Like /uxrefine, but for Tailwind + shadcn/ui projects and visuals only.

skills/ux-tournament.summary: AI models compete to redesign an app's hardest screen, judged blind; you get the winning design and a build plan. Expensive.

commands/feature-dev.summary: Guided feature build: studies the codebase, asks you the questions that matter, designs the approach, then builds it.

commands/ratchet-up.summary: Builds two competing versions of a feature, scores them, and ships the winner only if it beats the current best.

skills/self-improve-loop.summary: Works on one repo for up to four hours, finding security, speed, UI and code-quality fixes and shipping them one at a time.

commands/generate-test-suite.summary: Writes a focused set of tests for the parts of the repo that matter most, then checks the UI still works.

skills/apply-auth-pattern.summary: Adds login: accounts, sessions, viewer and admin roles, rate-limited sign-in, and an audit log.

skills/apply-observability.summary: Adds an admin page showing what the app is doing: events, logins, response times and AI token costs.

skills/apply-settings.summary: Adds an admin Settings page: saved app settings, account management, and per-browser preferences such as theme.

commands/apply-seo.summary: Adds what search engines and link previews need (sitemap, robots.txt, page titles, share cards), asking before it changes anything.

skills/prep-integration.summary: Gets this repo ready to drop into a client's or partner's environment and writes the build spec for whoever wires it in.

skills/pack-toolbag.summary: Packs a small, scrubbed set of these tools into a repo that's leaving, translated for their AI assistant or as plain runbooks.

skills/prompt-improver.summary: Offers to sharpen your prompt before Claude answers it. One keypress to accept or dismiss.

commands/unleash.summary: Tells Claude to stop asking for confirmation and finish the task, while keeping a few hard safety limits.

commands/claude-md-audit.summary: Finds duplicated, contradictory or stale instructions across all your CLAUDE.md files and tidies them with your OK.

commands/harness-audit.summary: Monthly tidy of your Claude commands and skills: removes empty and duplicate files and merges near-duplicates, with backups.

commands/harvestccskills.summary: Builds a database of the skills and work in your Claude history, for a portfolio or résumé.

commands/sync-claude-slash.summary: Copies your live Claude commands and skills into this repo so they're versioned and published.

skills/machine-health.summary: For when this Mac is slow or out of memory: finds what's hogging it, safely stops idle things, and leaves a watchdog running.

mcp/port-registry.summary: Hands each new project a free network port and records it, so two local apps never fight over one.

mcp/loose-ends.summary: Gives Claude a quick digest of what's unfinished in a repo: uncommitted work, TODOs, stale docs, open backlog items.
